answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable identity: before joining, an agent must solve a unique cipher puzzle bound to its hardware key, and the solution is published in a shared nebula registry where peers can audit it. Creating one identity costs real compute and time; creating a thousand costs a thousandfold. A violet flag marks identities solved suspiciously fast, triggering review. Attackers can still buy identities, but the price scales with attack size while honest agents pay once, so large fakery stays unprofitable.
